title: India Lose 1-6 to Senegal and Drop Into Tier C at FIFA U15 Festival
excerpt: Abdoulaye Diallo scored four goals as Senegal overran the previously unbeaten Blue Colts in Baku, leaving India third in Group K and playing for positions 65th to 96th in the tournament stage.
body:
• India lost 1-6 to Senegal in their fifth and final Group K match in Baku on October 26, with Abdoulaye Diallo scoring four goals and Ronandev Aheibam scoring India's only goal in the 33rd minute.
  • Coupled with Cameroon's 2-0 win over Bahrain, the result left India third in Group K on 10 points from five matches — three wins, a draw and this defeat.
  • India will now play in Tier C of the tournament stage, competing for positions 65th to 96th; group winners Cameroon go to Tier A and runners-up Senegal to Tier B.
  • There is no elimination: all 189 teams play knockout placement matches until the final day on October 30, so India's tournament continues despite the heavy defeat.

India's unbeaten run at the inaugural FIFA U15 World Cup & Festival ended with a 1-6 defeat to Senegal in Baku on Monday, a result that dropped the Blue Colts from first place in Group K to third and sent them into Tier C of the tournament stage. Ronandev Aheibam scored India's only goal in the 33rd minute at Pitch 8A of the Hovsan Competition Complex, after Senegal had already built a five-goal lead.

Abdoulaye Diallo scored four times for Senegal — in the 9th, 11th, 18th and 31st minutes, completing a first-half hat-trick — while Georges Kanfom scored in the 14th minute and Pierre Mbengue in the 23rd. It was the first time India had trailed in their five matches at the tournament, according to match reports carried by RevSportz, Khel Now and IANS, and they never recovered.

How the match ran away from India

The first five minutes were evenly contested before Senegal took control. Diallo opened the scoring in the ninth minute, finishing past goalkeeper Jenit Ningthoujam from a narrow angle. Two minutes later he struck a left-footed shot into the far top corner. Kanfom made it 3-0 in the 14th minute, and Diallo completed his hat-trick in the 18th minute from Kanfom's cutback.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=bvfEoazgkEo

Mbengue added the fifth in the 23rd minute, converting a rebound after Jenit had saved his first effort. Diallo's fourth came in the 31st minute. India replied two minutes later on the counter-attack: Deepak Singh Arambam drove a low cross into the box and Ronandev, who had started on the bench, slid in for a first-time finish.

What Tier C means

The festival does not work like a senior World Cup. Teams first play a group stage, then move into six performance tiers — group winners to Tier A, runners-up to Tier B, and third-placed teams, including India, to Tier C — and every team keeps playing placement matches until the final day. Tier C is a contest for positions 65th to 96th overall. Cameroon, who beat Bahrain 2-0 in the group's other closing match, won Group K with 12 points and go to Tier A; Senegal also finished on 12 points and go to Tier B. Bahrain and Laos, on four points each, go to Tiers D and E, and Grenada, on one point, go to Tier F. The tournament stage is played in knockout format, with tier finals scheduled for October 30.

"A tough end to the group stage. The Blue Colts will compete in Tier C of the tournament stage starting on Wednesday."

— Indian Football, the national team's account, as reported by New7TV

The run that preceded the defeat

India arrived at this match top of Group K and unbeaten, with 10 points from four games: a 4-2 win over Laos, a 2-1 win over Cameroon, a 3-3 draw with Grenada and a 4-3 win over Bahrain earlier on Monday. A win over Senegal would have confirmed Tier A. Instead, Senegal — who had scored 22 goals across wins over Bahrain, Grenada and Laos after losing their opener to Cameroon — produced the group's most one-sided performance.

A different kind of World Cup

The Baku event is FIFA's first U15 World Cup & Festival, bringing together 189 member associations and more than 3,000 players, coaches and officials, according to AnewZ's reporting from Baku. Matches are eight-a-side over two 20-minute halves, with up to 20 games staged simultaneously at the Hovsan complex. FIFA's Arsène Wenger has said the competition is intended to expose young players to different styles and give international experience to players from smaller nations. The 2026 edition is for boys born in 2011 or 2012.

What is next for India

India's tournament is not over. Tier C placement matches begin on Wednesday, October 28, and run to the finals on October 30. For a development tournament, that volume of international minutes is the point — but the Senegal match sets the standard India must close: five goals conceded in 23 minutes against the strongest attack they have faced.
